comments.text: MF map strip: 64 cells, one per world column, read as $0600,Y by resident $4173 and $3B51 (the map repeats through mask $3F). The low nibble of a cell selects its block type through the table at $073E. Columns 0 to 34 hold 06 00 00 02 00 01 00 03 00 01 00 04 00 01 00 05 00 06 00 02 00 01 00 04 00 01 00 03 01 00 00 05 00 01 06; the rest of the strip is zero.
192 bytes ($0640-$06FF) after the 64-cell strip, all zero except $06FF ($06). The map position is masked with $3F, so the scene never indexes these bytes.

Start of the 32-byte scene header that the loader at $557A unpacks after the map. The bytes are $50 46 2D 2D 00 02 40 0F 0C 0B 08 08 08 08 55 46. The loader reads $0701 ($46, "F") as the name character of the picture P and character set C resources it loads to $BC00 and $E000, $070F ($46, "F") as the name character of the overlay U loaded to $8B00, and $0703 ($2D, "-") as the extra costume selector, where a dash means none. $0700 and $0702 are not read by the loader.

Three numeric header bytes: $0704 (0) is the loop limit the loader compares at $568F and is read by the camera and motion routines, $0705 (2) indexes the tables at $59A1 and $59A8 that set $5E, $5F and $60, and $0706 (64) is halved into $02C8 and $02C7 at $566A.

Seven colour bytes ($0707-$070D = 0F 0C 0B 08 08 08 08) read by $5A34: $0708 and $0709 go to the VIC background colour registers $D022 and $D023, $0707 is cached at $02DD as the display colour, and $070A-$070D are copied to the four message palette bytes $6998-$699B.
Two bytes, "UF" ($55 $46): the overlay resource name, whose second character the loader compares with its cache at $508E and loads at $8B00 ($070F).

Ten bytes ($0710-$0719 = 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00): depth thresholds. $0710 is read by the object grid and placement routines ($37B4, $383F, $5487), $0711 at $548A, $0718 at $5397 and $0719 at $53B9.

Costume selector ($08), the index into the initial-animation table at $5985 read at $51EA and $5985. The three bytes after it ($071B-$071D = FF 03 FF) are read at $5201, $5207 and $51E4 when entry placement starts.
Sixteen replacement cell nibbles for OPEN, indexed by the current cell's low nibble. Bytes: 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F. Nibbles that change: none.
Sixteen replacement cell nibbles for CLOSE, indexed by the current cell's low nibble. Bytes: 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F. Nibbles that change: none.

Sixteen low-nibble-to-type values read by $4171/$4173 and $3B51 (bytes: 00 07 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00). Types $80 and above are negative; the engine falls back to depth-table index zero for them.

Sixteen inclusive upper column bounds read by $4115 (bytes: 05 09 0D 15 19 1C 21 FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF). Resident $411C takes the first entry whose bound is at least the coarse column, so each region is the span of columns up to its bound.
Sixteen zero bytes ($075E-$076D) between the column thresholds and the selectors. The scan at $411C stops at index 15 ($075D), so it does not read them.

Sixteen source selectors, one per region (bytes: 02 02 02 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00). Resident $412B reads the one for the region found at $411C: 0 uses the region itself as the table index (bank 0), 1 takes bits $60 of the state byte $0500, 2 takes bits $60 of $0501, and 3 or more take bits $60 of the shared PRNG. The selected bank (0 to 3) is offset 32 bytes per bank into the exit arrays.
Scene requests of bank 0, one per region ($077E-$078D): region 1 requests scene 11; region 3 requests scene 16; region 6 requests scene 16; the rest are zero. A request of 0 keeps the current scene.
